chunk_map.heading: (title) Codify the rules, place the file

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Referent resolution under a sequential deck read.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Sequential read across all 10 chunks. Closest candidates, all resolve: (a) chunk 3 line 31 'The same move you ran at M1 on a bug ticket, pointed at a story' -- module vocabulary unpacked in the same clause ('a bug ticket'); verified `close-the-ticket.md` (M1) L31 'A second bug ticket from a different part of the system' -- the referenced M1 beat is real. (b) chunk 8 line 88 'a branch from the second-pass read' -- resolves under the module-include-order carve-out: `push-back-on-the-plan.md` is the immediately-preceding exercise per `plan-mode-done-right.md` L34/36 include order, and establishes 'second-pass read'/'second read' repeatedly (L5, L54, L99, L105) -- verified present. (c) chunk 5 line 63 'the picked path' continues chunk 4's subject ('Decide the location with Claude', L46), ordinary same-topic hand-off across adjacent slides. (d) chunk 6 line 70 'Ask Claude what this file could drive later' -- 'this file' is the rules file established across chunks 1/3/4, term-reused-across-slides is the rule's own NOT-violation case. Body text at lines 1-111 is unchanged from the prior audited pass except L7 ('What you build' widget line, self-contained) and L66's header wording -- neither touches a referent.

No positional callback found. Chunk 3 L31 names M1 by module code plus unpacked content ('a bug ticket'), not by position. Chunk 5 L64's link is named by title -- '[Claude Code for engineers](...)' -- navigational-pointer carve-out. Chunk 8 L88 names 'the second-pass read' by its own descriptor, not by position relative to this file.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Live-demo beats survive a text read.
rules_evaluated.na_reason: no guess-before-reveal or trainer-only-scene construction; grep for guess|predict|reveal on the body returns one unrelated past-tense hit (L104 'a convention it guessed')

rules_evaluated.evidence: Shortest chunk: chunk 2 (L25-28), one bullet -- 'The rule that arrives generic, like "pick tasks that span multiple files," is the one to rewrite in your words, or reject.' -- a complete, self-carrying directive with a concrete example, not a wait-state fragment. Every other chunk carries >=2 bullets, a table, or framing prose plus a prompt fence.

Checked all 9 `##` headers against chunk content. Closest candidate: chunk 6's header changed to 'Phase 3: Explore what this file could automate later' (L66) -- content (L70 'Ask Claude what this file could drive later', plus the automation-shapes prompt) matches the new header at least as well as the old, no contradiction introduced. Chunk 9's Phase-label pattern (names the frame; body explains applying it) holds as before.

`grep -nE '\bNot [A-Z]'` on the body (L1-111) -> 0 hits. `grep -niE 'most useful|one of the|best way|game.chang|essential|crucial'` -> 0 hits. Numerals present are only widget-chrome time budgets (L3, 15, 41, 68, 82, 100) with no retraction/hedge attached. No anaphora/epistrophe triple or empty-leg verb triplet found on manual read of every bullet, including the new L7 wording.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Internal dialect never lands on a slide.
rules_evaluated.evidence: `grep -niE '\bsurface\b|\bfiring\b|\bcompendium\b|forcing function|\bbeat\b|\bmood\b|\bConnections\b'` on the body (L1-111) -> one hit, L5 'surface task-shaping rules from the session you just ran' -- the exempted ordinary engineering VERB use, not the noun 'writing surface'. No other dialect terms present.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Emphasis budget -- bold is for handles, and go very lightly.
rules_evaluated.evidence: `grep -nE '\*\*[A-Za-z][^*]{0,60}\*\*'` on the body -> bold only at widget chrome (L3,5,7,9, exempt) and chunk 9 L104-106: '**Planning gaps.**', '**Conflicting information.**', '**Other context.**' -- three bolded checklist-item handles, each within the <=5-word span cap, on one slide against the default <=1-per-slide budget. The prior pass's REVISE turned on the maintainer block CONTRADICTING the body ('no bolded handles... all bullet leads plain'). That contradiction is now resolved: the maintainer block's emphasis-budget note (L134 of the maintainer section, cross-referenced to the dated 'Phase 5 Boy Scout slide (Antti-directed 2026-08-23; moved here 2026-08-25)' note) now explicitly names the three bullets, attributes them to Antti, and states the slide is scanned for a match rather than read through -- a dated, on-passage accept-note per the dispatch preamble's instruction to check for one before flagging. Per-preamble discipline: a documented accept-note is not re-litigated as a fresh REVISE.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Presence precedes content -- verify against the composed deck, not long-read.
rules_evaluated.evidence: `grep -n "extract-the-task-shaping-rule" curriculum/trainings/agentic-engineering-101/plan-mode-done-right.md` -> L36 '[Exercise: Extract the task-shaping rule](exercises/extract-the-task-shaping-rule.md)', a standard exercise-include reaching the composed deck through the module's `.phase--exercise` wrapper. Not a phase-less prework/supplementary/reference section.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Heading grammar is the mood switch, and it is load-bearing.
rules_evaluated.evidence: All 9 headers checked against the exercise grammar (imperative or phase label). 5 Phase-labels (L13,39,66,80,98) and 4 imperative/catalogue headers (L25, L29, L75). Chunk 6's reworded header 'Phase 3: Explore what this file could automate later' remains a Phase label with an imperative lead verb, same shape as before. L51 'Where rules can live, and when they load' matches the explicit non-violation carve-out 'catalogue entries naming their subject'.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: A bullet earns its slot or dies -- three classes that read as rigour and carry nothing.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Read every bullet against the three low-value classes. Closest candidates: (a) chunk 8 L92 blockquote 'Precise prompting is harder than it looks' sits inside a genuinely actionable recovery warning followed by two more sentences of real instruction -- not a slide-closing kicker. (b) chunk 9 L102 'A rule in your file is one way to compound a session' pivots M1-earned compounding to repo-level context gaps rather than re-announcing an already-landed lens -- same-move-different-face, not doctrine restatement. No self-referential design commentary found anywhere in body.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: A retitled slide re-earns its bullets against the new header.
rules_evaluated.evidence: The one header change since the pin (chunk 6, L66: 'Phase 3: What this file could automate later' -> 'Phase 3: Explore what this file could automate later') is a lead-verb insertion, not a job change -- the slide's promise (naming what the rules file could later drive) is identical before and after. Body under it (L70 'Ask Claude what this file could drive later', the automation-shapes prompt, and the 'Read the shapes' follow-on) answers both wordings equally; no inherited bullet answers an old job the new header dropped. `git diff 9edae2ef..HEAD` shows no other `##` line changed with its body left untouched.
